sources.title: MPS says Intesa's bid financially fair but does not fully reflect prospective value
Spain to extend banking tax to fund housing policies, PM says
Latest EU budget proposal is very disappointing, French presidency says
EU ban on plastic waste exports to non-OECD takes effect
Singaporean extradited to face US charges over global insider trading scheme

stories.topic: ITALY / EUROPE / INTESA SANPAOLO / MONTE DEI PASCHI / MEDIOBANCA / BANKS / MERGERS AND ACQUISITIONS
stories.headline: MPS judges Intesa Sanpaolo offer financially fair while disputing its share of future value
stories.body: Reuters reported MPS's qualified assessment of Intesa Sanpaolo's EUR34.5bn (about US$38bn) takeover offer. Advisers judged the improved price fair as of 18 November, but MPS said it did not fully capture prospective value from its Mediobanca acquisition. The board unanimously approved the position after a director resigned amid disagreement. The shareholder tender phase starts Tuesday, 24 November. This assessment is distinct from approval or completion of the acquisition. No directly attributable share-price or credit-spread movement was verified.
stories.analysis: Banking consolidation still faces valuation, distribution-of-benefits and execution questions; an assessment of financial fairness does not settle them.
stories.watch_next: Tender participation from 24 November, revised terms and regulatory decisions.

stories.topic: SPAIN / PEDRO SANCHEZ / SANTANDER / BBVA / CAIXABANK / BANKS / TAX / HOUSING / FISCAL POLICY
stories.headline: Spain proposes a 2027 bank-levy extension to support housing
stories.body: Reuters reported that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez plans cabinet approval on Tuesday for extending Spain's banking levy through 2027. He estimated EUR1.4bn in tax receipts for social housing, tenant tax incentives and home renovation. The levy spans 1%-7% of net interest income and commissions by lending-income volume; the 7% tier mainly affects Santander, BBVA and CaixaBank. These are proposed policy and anticipated tax receipts, not confirmed collections or a realised banking loss. No attributable bank-share, bond-spread or euro movement was established.
stories.analysis: An extension could affect bank earnings and retained capital, while its final legal scope and implementation remain material.
stories.watch_next: Cabinet decision, final scope and actual revenue collection.

stories.topic: EUROPEAN UNION / FRANCE / ANTONIO COSTA / FISCAL POLICY / AGRICULTURE / BUDGET NEGOTIATIONS
stories.headline: France rejects the current EU 2028-2034 budget negotiating proposal
stories.body: Reuters reported that the French presidency rejected European Council President Antonio Costa's latest proposal for the EU's 2028-2034 budget as an inadequate basis for agreement. France highlighted insufficient agricultural support and protection of farmers' incomes. The budget funds policies including farming, industry, technology and research. This is a negotiating position on future spending, not an approved reduction or a new monetary-policy decision. No directly attributable sovereign-spread, Bund-yield or euro movement was verified.
stories.analysis: Prolonged negotiations could affect the allocation and timing of future EU spending; the draft remains subject to agreement.
stories.watch_next: Revised text, other member-state positions and eventual budget agreement.

stories.topic: EUROPEAN UNION / MALAYSIA / INDONESIA / VIETNAM / TRADE / ENVIRONMENT / RECYCLING / REGULATION
stories.headline: EU plastic-waste export restrictions take effect for non-OECD destinations
stories.body: Reuters reported on 20 November that the EU prohibition on plastic-waste exports to non-OECD destinations takes effect on 21 November, alongside tighter scrutiny of OECD shipments. Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam are among the affected destination countries. Reuters cited 1.5 million metric tonnes of total EU plastic-waste exports annually; that is not the volume sent to those three countries alone. Wider non-OECD waste-export restrictions are scheduled for 21 May 2027, with conditional exceptions under the regulation. No attributable FX or listed-recycler price move was verified.
stories.analysis: Regional recyclers may face supply and compliance changes; the legal change does not establish a measured loss or investment return.
stories.watch_next: Customs enforcement, destination trade flows and recycler supply adjustments.

stories.topic: SINGAPORE / UNITED STATES / SECURITIES / INSIDER TRADING / REGULATORY AND LEGAL / COMPLIANCE
stories.headline: Singaporean extradited to face United States insider-trading charges; allegations remain unproven
stories.body: Reuters reported on 20 November that a Singaporean appeared in Boston federal court after extradition to face securities-fraud and money-laundering charges. A Singapore court ruling preceded the extradition. Prosecutors allege an insider-trading network used confidential corporate and acquisition information from 2016 to 2024, including tips from bankers and corporate insiders. His lawyer said he would plead not guilty. Arraignment is scheduled for 16 December. These are charges, not convictions; the report does not establish misconduct by a specific Singapore bank. No attributable market-price or credit-spread reaction was verified.
stories.analysis: The case illustrates cross-border enforcement and protection of confidential corporate information without establishing the allegations as proven facts.
stories.watch_next: Court proceedings and confirmed regulatory findings.
